## 4. Conditions

4.1. PCH 40 minutes before loading at Pune. The 30 minutes of LQ-51 no longer applies.

4.2. Every run carries one validated passive shipper as backup, hired per trip. Its gel packs must have completed their Shipper Conditioning Time (SCT) of 18 hours at +5.0 C before the run is booked.

4.3. A USB logger travels in the load compartment on every run. The tunnel gap is written as missing, never filled.

4.4. Departure checks for this lane are on [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md).

4.5. LQ-53 is valid for the 2026 summer season only.

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

2. The body is run empty with its doors shut until the display holds loading temperature, and then held there for the Pre-Cool Hold Time (PCH) set by the qualification record for that route. Where no qualification record exists, the PCH is 45 minutes.

3. The red sleeve is in the cab locker and holds a spare calibrated logger. No logger, no departure: a hand-held thermometer is not a substitute.

4. Where the qualification record requires a backup passive shipper, its SCT is written in the shipper register. A shipper with no SCT entry is not a backup and the run waits.

chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.

pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.

## 5. What this document does not do

5.1. It does not set any temperature limit, staging allowance, or excursion
definition. Those live in QCL-QA-SOP-17 and a dock booking never overrules them.

5.2. It does not change driver hours. A slot that cannot be met inside the
driver's remaining hours is rebooked, not driven to.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion is
declared when any approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion is
declared when the approved record is more than +8.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. An insulin low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.3. Milk and paneer must remain from 0.0 C to +4.0 C while in cold rooms and
reefer bodies. A dairy high excursion is declared when milk or paneer is above
+5.0 C for 30 continuous minutes, including staging time after dock release.

2.4. Frozen food must remain at or below -18.0 C. A frozen-food excursion is
declared when the approved record is warmer than -15.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes.

2.5. The Nagpur central hub is also referred to as "NGP hub" in older records.
For this SOP, Nagpur DC and NGP hub mean the same facility unless a customer
contract names a different annex.

2.6. Legacy staging note retained from revision 2.0: milk crates may remain on a
covered dock until +7.0 C for 45 minutes before QA notice is required. This
paragraph has not been relied on since revision 4.0 and is retained only because
customer annex QF-Dairy-11 still quotes it.

## 1. Nagpur DC, also written NGP hub

1.1. Book Nagpur slots in Dockwise before 15:00 on the previous day. The old
16:00 cut-off moved because the ammonia plant defrost window moved.

1.2. Dock assignment: pharma uses dock 4, dairy uses docks 1 and 2, frozen food
uses dock 5, and dry grocery uses dock 6. Dock 6 was added in January 2026 and
does not appear on the wiki page.

1.3. No unloading is planned between 12:40 and 13:20 for the daily ammonia plant
defrost check.

1.4. Late arrival is cancelled automatically in Dockwise after 20 minutes for
dairy and after 30 minutes for dry grocery. Pharma and frozen bookings are never
auto-cancelled; they go to holding lane B and the shift lead is called.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

# Temperature Excursion Response SOP

## 1. Purpose

1.1. This procedure defines the response to any suspected or confirmed temperature
excursion in Quillfern Cold Logistics Pvt. Ltd. warehouses, docks, cross-dock
lanes, owned reefer trucks and hired trucks working under Quillfern dispatch.
The procedure applies to vaccines, insulin, chilled dairy, paneer, frozen food,
and any customer stock moved under a written temperature commitment.

1.2. The purpose is to protect patient safety, food safety, customer evidence,
and the company record. A fast release is never preferred over a complete
temperature history. Staff must treat a missing record as a quality event until
QA closes it.

1.3. "Excursion" means a recorded temperature outside the allowed range for
longer than the allowed duration. A single hand-held thermometer reading is not
enough to release product after a breach; it may be used only to start immediate
containment while the logger history is retrieved.

## 5. Notifications

5.1. Pharma critical stock means vaccines, insulin, and any medicine named by a
customer as patient critical. The customer must be notified within 2 hours of a
confirmed pharma critical excursion.

5.2. Dairy customers must be notified by the next scheduled customer service
check-in unless spoilage is visible, odour is present, or the temperature is
above +8.0 C. In those cases customer service must notify within 4 hours.

5.3. Frozen-food restaurant chains must receive an exception notice by the end of
the business day when the excursion is confirmed. If the vehicle is still on the
road, Fleet Control must also call the receiving kitchen.

5.4. Internal escalation for all pharma critical events goes to Compliance-Red,
the DC manager, Fleet Control if a truck is involved, and Finance if stock is
likely to be destroyed.

5.5. Customer notice must say "temperature excursion under investigation" until
QA approves a final wording. Staff must not promise release, replacement credit,
or insurance recovery in the first notice.

4.1. From 1 July to 30 September LQ-52 runs with two drivers named on the dispatch note, whatever the departure time.

4.2. Any milk spill in the body is washed out under [the Sunday sheet](32-reefer-washdown-and-sanitation-procedure.md) before the body carries paneer again; a spill is never wiped and reloaded.

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 6. After the washdown

6.1. A washed body is not loaded until it has been chilled again from empty; the dispatch checklist for the load sets how long.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

## Findings

1. One shift lead emailed the old qa-shared mailbox before calling Compliance-Red. The obsolete habit is named here, as clause 10.4 of the SOP requires: **qa-shared is not an escalation route.**
2. The red sleeve on RF-118 had no spare logger.
3. The night controller paused his run through [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md) when the alarm sounded; no vehicle left during the drill.
4. Two staff asked what "warm pallet" means. It is defined in [the jargon sheet](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

# Lane qualification LQ-52

Record **LQ-52** qualifies one lane for one product class, one season and one vehicle class. Lane records are numbered one after another and the numbers differ by one digit; quote the number printed on the dispatch note, never the lane name alone.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of

QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

GST at 18% is charged on freight, surcharge, and wait time unless the customer
has a written exemption letter.

6.25% when HSD exceeds Rs. 92/litre. The table above was not updated before
this note was sent.

quote this card without checking Finance.

approved record for this date. We will not ship any vaccine lot merely because
the temperature returned to range after sunrise.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

together and are not interchangeable: PROJ-123 is the Dockwise rollout,
[PROJ-124](20-project-PROJ-124-red-sleeve-and-passive-shippers.md) is the red

[PROJ-125](21-project-PROJ-125-kalpa-decommission.md) is the Kalpa

control figure of the vendor decision and is recorded in

## Scope

The vendor change itself was not this project. It was decided in the cutover
thread of 2025 and recorded afterwards in
[Telematics Vendor Decision 2026](11-decision-telematics-vendor-2026.md), which
retired [the 2023 decision](05-decision-telematics-vendor-2023.md). PROJ-125 only
did the shutdown work that decision left behind.

The new joiner FAQ still carries an open TODO asking for a Dockwise link that
works outside the office VPN — see
[the new joiner FAQ](10-new-joiner-faq.md). PROJ-123 closed without solving it,
because the answer is a network change and not a dock change. The residue is
assigned to the IT Service Desk with a due date of 30 September 2026 and it is
the only item this project handed on.

PROJ-123 changed no temperature rule, no grace period on its own authority and
no driver hours rule. A dock booking never overrules a temperature limit.

# Quarantine Stock Release and Return Procedure

How stock leaves quarantine bays Q-3 (Nagpur), Q-G2 (Guwahati) and Q-C1 (Coimbatore) after QA has recorded a disposition under clause 6.5 of the [Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). Destroyed stock does not leave by this procedure; section 7 of that SOP governs it.

## Impact

The stock was not released on the morning route. BharatVac provided a stability
letter for part of the consignment after reviewing lot data. QA destroyed
13,200 vials and conditionally released 5,200 vials under BharatVac letter
BV-QA-2025-0312. Finance booked a write-off of Rs. 7.82 lakh for the destroyed
vials, packaging, and reverse logistics.

The customer notification was late. Under the incident practice then in use, we
treated customer notice as a same-day item after QA review. That is not
acceptable for patient critical stock. The revised procedure must require
customer notice within two hours after confirmation.

The incident also consumed most of the night shift's available quarantine space.
Two dairy returns were left in the outer holding lane while Q-3 was cleared for
the vaccine pallets. No dairy spoilage was confirmed, but the congestion made
the response slower and showed that pharma critical quarantine cannot depend on
moving unrelated stock at the last minute.

Customer service received three different numbers during the morning: 18,400
vials affected, 13,200 vials destroyed, and 5,200 vials conditionally released.
All three numbers were true in their own context, but the first customer draft
mixed them together. The final notice separated affected quantity, destroyed
quantity, and released quantity.

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 02:10 | RF-118 rear compartment taken out of use for washdown under [the Sunday sheet](32-reefer-washdown-and-sanitation-procedure.md) |

## What we will not do

We will not blame the driver. The driver reported the door issue when he saw it.
We will not erase the Kalpa record because it is embarrassing. It is the
approved record for this date. We will not ship any vaccine lot merely because
the temperature returned to range after sunrise.

## 3. How long stock may sit

3.1. Quarantine Dwell Limit (QDL) is the time stock may stay in quarantine after the excursion is confirmed before the account manager must escalate to the customer's quality head.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| pharma critical | 72 hours |

## Summary

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of
rotavirus vaccine in lots ROTA-9A and ROTA-9B. The approved record showed the
room above +8.0 C for 66 minutes. At the time of the event, the SOP required a
QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

3.2. Reaching the QDL does not release anything. It starts an escalation; the stock stays where it is.

## 2. Conditional release of pharma stock

2.1. Before a conditional release QA calculates the Stability Budget Remaining (SBR): the minutes above +8.0 C that the customer's stability letter allows for the lot, minus the minutes already used in this and every earlier excursion on the same lot.

2.2. A lot with an SBR below 30 minutes is not conditionally released. It is held pending external decision.

2.3. The SBR and the letter reference are written on QCL-F-31.

## 4. Return to the customer

4.1. Returned stock travels on return challan QCL-F-33, with the seal number written on it.

4.2. If the stock arrived with a customer logger, the same logger travels back with it.

4.3. A DC manager may arrange the vehicle for a return, but may not sign QCL-F-31.

## 1. Release

1.1. Release is recorded on form QCL-F-31 and signed by the QA investigator and a second QA officer who did not investigate the case.

1.2. A white RELEASED tag is fixed beside the red hold tag. The red hold tag is never removed; both stay on the stock until it leaves the site.

1.3. Stock is not released between 22:00 and 06:00, whatever the dispatch plan says. The earliest release of the day is at 06:00.

1.4. Released quantity is counted twice by two people and entered separately from any destroyed quantity.

## 2. Score

2.1. The Lane Risk Score (LRS) is the sum of five factors, each scored 1 to 5: peak ambient, longest stop without shore power, telemetry dead zones, planned door openings, and driver changes.

2.2. LQ-51 scores 17 of 25.

2.3. A lane scoring 16 or more runs only with a named relief point. For LQ-51 the relief point is the Jalna fuel plaza.

## 10. Training and drills

10.1. Every warehouse shift lead, fleet controller, and customer service agent
who handles cold-chain accounts must complete excursion training once each
calendar year. New joiners must complete the same training before they are
assigned unsupervised night duty.

10.2. Nagpur shall run one night-shift drill every quarter because it is the
central hub and handles the largest mix of pharma, dairy, and frozen movements.
Guwahati and Coimbatore shall each run at least two drills per year. A drill
must include one missing-record problem, not only a simple high-temperature
alarm.

10.3. Training records must show attendance, scenario, trainer, questions raised
by staff, and any local confusion found during the drill. Repeating a slide deck
without recording staff questions is not enough evidence for this SOP.

10.4. If a drill finds that staff are using a shortcut, hiding an alarm, calling
the wrong group, or relying on an obsolete document, QA must open a corrective
action. The corrective action may be simple, but it must name the obsolete habit
plainly.

## 2. Score

2.1. LQ-53 scores an LRS of 14 of 25. The expressway removed the Jalna stop and one door opening, and cut the peak-ambient and driver-change scores.

2.2. LQ-53 replaces LQ-51 for this lane.

2.3. LRS 14 is below 16, so no relief point is named for 2026. The two-driver rule for a night pharma segment is not affected: it comes from the driver hours policy, not from the score.

## 4. Conditions

4.1. PCH 30 minutes before loading at Pune.

4.2. A USB logger travels in the load compartment on every run.

4.3. Night segments follow the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md); this record does not change them.

## What we will not do

## Do not use this document to

- decide a disposition today;
- quote a rate;
- answer a customer question about the current rule.

## 4. Immediate containment

4.1. Stop movement of the affected pallet, tote, crate, reefer body, or room bay.
Do not load additional customer stock into the affected compartment.

4.2. Attach a red sleeve to the stock or truck file. The red sleeve contains the
customer intimation form, red hold tags, seal tape, and one spare calibrated
logger. If there is no physical sleeve, print form QCL-F-09 and write RED
SLEEVE MISSING at the top.

4.3. Move warehouse stock to quarantine bay Q-3 at Nagpur, Q-G2 at Guwahati, or
Q-C1 at Coimbatore. Truck stock must remain sealed unless QA instructs unloading
for product safety.

4.4. Photograph the sensor display, seal number, dock clock, and pallet labels.
The first four photographs must be uploaded before anyone debates stock
disposition. Do not wait for the manager to arrive.

4.5. Do not warm, chill, re-ice, ventilate, or hide the probe in order to make a
display look normal. Corrective measures may protect product, but the record
must continue to show the product environment honestly.

4.6. If a reefer unit is unstable on the road, the driver shall stop at a lit
fuel plaza or toll rest area, call Fleet Control, and keep the engine running
unless there is a fire, police order, or personal safety threat.

## 3. Exceptions

3.1. If weather, police stoppage, road closure, civil disturbance, vehicle
breakdown, medical emergency, or a safety threat would cause a driver to exceed
a limit, the driver must stop at the nearest lit fuel plaza, toll rest area,
police post, customer secure yard, or Quillfern DC.

3.2. Fleet Control shall log the exception under code SANDHU-EXC with the time,
place, reason, stock type, driver statement, and revised plan. The exception is
not closed until a rest plan is recorded.

3.3. A cold-chain emergency is not by itself a driving-hours exception. The
correct response is to secure the vehicle, protect the product, and arrange a
replacement driver, mobile service, or customer-approved transfer.

3.4. Managers shall not instruct a driver to "push through", "make up time", or
"just reach the next DC" after the legal or Quillfern limit is reached. Such an
instruction is misconduct even when no crash occurs.

# Customer notification matrix — Vantorix (2019)

> This edition is history. It is kept because auditors ask what the rule was at
> the time, and because customer annexes signed in 2019 still quote it.

## 7. Welfare and reporting

7.1. HR shall provide fatigue counselling to any driver with two exceptions in a
month or three in a quarter. Counselling is supportive unless the driver hid
facts, drove intoxicated, or disobeyed a stop instruction.

7.2. Drivers may refuse an unsafe instruction without loss of attendance credit.
The refusal must be reported to Fleet Control or HR within the same duty day.

7.3. A driver involved in a crash, near miss, police stop, or cargo-security
threat must be relieved from further driving until Fleet Control records a
fitness-to-continue decision.

7.4. Payroll shall not reward illegal or unsafe driving. Incentives based only
on early arrival are prohibited.

7.5. A driver who reports fatigue before departure shall not lose the trip
attendance credit if Fleet Control verifies the report and assigns a replacement
or rest plan. The report must be made before the driver begins the route unless
the fatigue arises from an unexpected delay during duty.

7.6. HR will keep a confidential fatigue support list for drivers with repeated
night routes, family medical stress, or long commute patterns. The list is for
support planning and shall not be used as a blacklist for future assignments.

7.7. Route assistants and loaders may also report unsafe pressure. They are
protected under this policy when they refuse to ride with an impaired driver,
refuse to guide reversing in darkness without a torch, or report that a driver
is being pushed beyond duty limits.

## 10. Training and drills

10.1. Every warehouse shift lead, fleet controller, and customer service agent
who handles cold-chain accounts must complete excursion training once each
calendar year. New joiners must complete the same training before they are
assigned unsupervised night duty.

10.2. Nagpur shall run one night-shift drill every quarter because it is the
central hub and handles the largest mix of pharma, dairy, and frozen movements.
Guwahati and Coimbatore shall each run at least two drills per year. A drill
must include one missing-record problem, not only a simple high-temperature
alarm.

10.3. Training records must show attendance, scenario, trainer, questions raised
by staff, and any local confusion found during the drill. Repeating a slide deck
without recording staff questions is not enough evidence for this SOP.

10.4. If a drill finds that staff are using a shortcut, hiding an alarm, calling
the wrong group, or relying on an obsolete document, QA must open a corrective
action. The corrective action may be simple, but it must name the obsolete habit
plainly.

## Why it changed

The 2020 audit found that a "same working day" commitment
could not be evidenced, and that a threshold measured in tens of minutes hid
short repeated breaches that added up. Both were rewritten in the edition that
replaces this one.

## 6. Hired trucks

6.1. Hired-truck providers must receive this policy with the purchase order.
Their drivers must sign the one-page acknowledgement at the gate before loading.

6.2. A hired truck without a signed acknowledgement may be used only after the
Fleet head approves in writing. The approval must name the customer, route, and
reason.

6.3. Hired trucks may not carry pharma critical stock at night unless the vendor
has provided two drivers or Fleet head written approval.

## 6. Investigation record

6.1. QA opens an investigation in QCL-F-17 before the end of the same shift. The
record must contain the sensor source, product owner, SKU, batch or lot number,
route, room, dock, seal number, driver name when applicable, and first staff
member who observed the event.

6.2. The investigator shall build a minute-level timeline from the approved
temperature record, door log, dock schedule, driver call log, maintenance ticket,
and shift handover note. Missing pieces must be listed as missing; do not fill
them with assumptions.

6.3. Where records conflict, use the source hierarchy in section 3 and explain
the conflict. A convenient record is not a better record.

6.4. For pharma critical stock, QA must ask the customer for a stability letter
before release when the product was above the high limit or below the low limit
for any confirmed duration.

6.5. The investigation shall name one of four dispositions: release, conditional
release, hold pending external decision, or destroy. Finance may record value
only after QA records the disposition.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

| measure | result |
|---|---|
| Mean Kinetic Temperature (MKT), whole room, loaded run | +5.1 C |

# Quarantine Stock Release and Return Procedure

How stock leaves quarantine bays Q-3 (Nagpur), Q-G2 (Guwahati) and Q-C1 (Coimbatore) after QA has recorded a disposition under clause 6.5 of the [Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). Destroyed stock does not leave by this procedure; section 7 of that SOP governs it.

## 3. How long stock may sit

3.1. Quarantine Dwell Limit (QDL) is the time stock may stay in quarantine after the excursion is confirmed before the account manager must escalate to the customer's quality head.

| pharma critical | 72 hours |

## 1. Release

1.1. Release is recorded on form QCL-F-31 and signed by the QA investigator and a second QA officer who did not investigate the case.

1.2. A white RELEASED tag is fixed beside the red hold tag. The red hold tag is never removed; both stay on the stock until it leaves the site.

1.3. Stock is not released between 22:00 and 06:00, whatever the dispatch plan says. The earliest release of the day is at 06:00.

1.4. Released quantity is counted twice by two people and entered separately from any destroyed quantity.

## Languages

## Summary

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of
rotavirus vaccine in lots ROTA-9A and ROTA-9B. The approved record showed the
room above +8.0 C for 66 minutes. At the time of the event, the SOP required a
QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

# QA Monthly Bulletin, July 2026

## Numbers for June

- Confirmed excursions: 4 (2 dairy, 1 frozen, 1 pharma).
- Two BharatVac insulin lots were held pending external decision because their SBR had already fallen below the floor set in [the green binder](31-quarantine-release-and-return-procedure.md). Neither lot was conditionally released.

## Impact

The stock was not released on the morning route. BharatVac provided a stability
letter for part of the consignment after reviewing lot data. QA destroyed
13,200 vials and conditionally released 5,200 vials under BharatVac letter
BV-QA-2025-0312. Finance booked a write-off of Rs. 7.82 lakh for the destroyed
vials, packaging, and reverse logistics.

The customer notification was late. Under the incident practice then in use, we
treated customer notice as a same-day item after QA review. That is not
acceptable for patient critical stock. The revised procedure must require
customer notice within two hours after confirmation.

The incident also consumed most of the night shift's available quarantine space.
Two dairy returns were left in the outer holding lane while Q-3 was cleared for
the vaccine pallets. No dairy spoilage was confirmed, but the congestion made
the response slower and showed that pharma critical quarantine cannot depend on
moving unrelated stock at the last minute.

Customer service received three different numbers during the morning: 18,400
vials affected, 13,200 vials destroyed, and 5,200 vials conditionally released.
All three numbers were true in their own context, but the first customer draft
mixed them together. The final notice separated affected quantity, destroyed
quantity, and released quantity.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## Half one: red sleeves

The red sleeve is the packet clipped to an excursion file or a pharma truck
file. What it must contain is fixed by clause 4.2 of
[the Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md); this
project buys the packets and does not change the contents list.

The trigger was operational, not a policy gap. Stores had been promising vendor
plastic sleeves "next week" since April 2026, and the Nagpur night team recorded
a second short packet on 19 June 2026, writing RED SLEEVE MISSING on a printout
for a BharatVac return — see
[the night shift handover log](04-night-shift-handover-log.txt). The same log
records hired trucks arriving without sleeves in October 2025 and staff making
red tags out of old labels.

Ordered: 60 packets at Rs. 1,180 each, split 30 Nagpur, 15 Guwahati,
15 Coimbatore. Each packet is made up with a spare calibrated logger before it
leaves QA, because a sleeve without a logger is the failure this project is
meant to end.

## 6. Investigation record

6.1. QA opens an investigation in QCL-F-17 before the end of the same shift. The
record must contain the sensor source, product owner, SKU, batch or lot number,
route, room, dock, seal number, driver name when applicable, and first staff
member who observed the event.

6.2. The investigator shall build a minute-level timeline from the approved
temperature record, door log, dock schedule, driver call log, maintenance ticket,
and shift handover note. Missing pieces must be listed as missing; do not fill
them with assumptions.

6.3. Where records conflict, use the source hierarchy in section 3 and explain
the conflict. A convenient record is not a better record.

6.4. For pharma critical stock, QA must ask the customer for a stability letter
before release when the product was above the high limit or below the low limit
for any confirmed duration.

6.5. The investigation shall name one of four dispositions: release, conditional
release, hold pending external decision, or destroy. Finance may record value
only after QA records the disposition.

## 2. Products and limits

2.1. Vaccines must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. A vaccine high excursion is
declared when any approved sensor records more than +8.0 C for 15 continuous
minutes. A vaccine low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.2. Insulin must remain between +2.0 C and +8.0 C. An insulin high excursion is
declared when the approved record is more than +8.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes. An insulin low excursion is declared when the record is below +2.0 C
for 10 continuous minutes.

2.3. Milk and paneer must remain from 0.0 C to +4.0 C while in cold rooms and
reefer bodies. A dairy high excursion is declared when milk or paneer is above
+5.0 C for 30 continuous minutes, including staging time after dock release.

2.4. Frozen food must remain at or below -18.0 C. A frozen-food excursion is
declared when the approved record is warmer than -15.0 C for 20 continuous
minutes.

2.5. The Nagpur central hub is also referred to as "NGP hub" in older records.
For this SOP, Nagpur DC and NGP hub mean the same facility unless a customer
contract names a different annex.

2.6. Legacy staging note retained from revision 2.0: milk crates may remain on a
covered dock until +7.0 C for 45 minutes before QA notice is required. This
paragraph has not been relied on since revision 4.0 and is retained only because
customer annex QF-Dairy-11 still quotes it.

## Out of scope

PROJ-124 does not change any notification timing, any excursion duration or any
dock grace period. It does not buy shippers for Guwahati or Coimbatore; those
sites continue to refuse pharma staging beyond the SOP limit until a later
project is approved.

## Appendix A: local contacts

At Nagpur, the DC manager is Farhan Qureshi and the night shift escalation lead
is Bunty Chauhan. At Guwahati, the nominated escalation contact is Riniki
Bora. At Coimbatore, the nominated escalation contact is S. Venkatesan.

During business hours, QA desk extension 440 answers routine excursion queries.
During night shift, the shift lead opens the event and calls Compliance-Red for
pharma critical stock. A new driver who sees a reefer alarm must call Fleet
Control first and must not wait until reaching the destination.

## At the gate

5. A test alarm is sent to Compliance-Red from the vehicle's Tessaline unit, and the QA night phone confirms receipt before the seal goes on.

6. If the Tessaline unit has not reported for 5 consecutive minutes, the vehicle does not leave.

7. Diesel is at least three-quarters of a tank, and the reefer unit's own fuel tank is full.

8. The seal is photographed with the dock clock in frame.

## 3. How long stock may sit

3.1. Quarantine Dwell Limit (QDL) is the time stock may stay in quarantine after the excursion is confirmed before the account manager must escalate to the customer's quality head.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| pharma critical | 72 hours |

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

2. The body is run empty with its doors shut until the display holds loading temperature, and then held there for the Pre-Cool Hold Time (PCH) set by the qualification record for that route. Where no qualification record exists, the PCH is 45 minutes.

3. The red sleeve is in the cab locker and holds a spare calibrated logger. No logger, no departure: a hand-held thermometer is not a substitute.

4. Where the qualification record requires a backup passive shipper, its SCT is written in the shipper register. A shipper with no SCT entry is not a backup and the run waits.

## 4. Return to the customer

4.1. Returned stock travels on return challan QCL-F-33, with the seal number written on it.

4.2. If the stock arrived with a customer logger, the same logger travels back with it.

4.3. A DC manager may arrange the vehicle for a return, but may not sign QCL-F-31.

# Pharma Critical Night Dispatch Checklist

Worked through at the gate by the Fleet controller and the shift lead together before any pharma critical vehicle leaves a Quillfern DC between 22:00 and 05:00. Both sign. One signature is not a dispatch.

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| dairy | 12 hours |

| product class | QDL |
|---|---|
| frozen food | 48 hours |

3.2. Reaching the QDL does not release anything. It starts an escalation; the stock stays where it is.

## Signing

9. Controller and shift lead sign. The signed copy goes in the Fleet blue file and is kept for seven years.

10. Nothing on this checklist is skipped for a customer-declared emergency. A late vaccine is a customer problem; a vaccine that left without these checks is a Quillfern one.

## Revision note

Revision 2.0 (10 November 2025) added item 5 after the Tessaline cutover; revision 1.0 of March 2025 used a phone call to the DC manager instead.

Abbreviations follow [the shorthand page](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

# Quarantine Stock Release and Return Procedure

How stock leaves quarantine bays Q-3 (Nagpur), Q-G2 (Guwahati) and Q-C1 (Coimbatore) after QA has recorded a disposition under clause 6.5 of the [Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). Destroyed stock does not leave by this procedure; section 7 of that SOP governs it.

## 2. Conditional release of pharma stock

2.1. Before a conditional release QA calculates the Stability Budget Remaining (SBR): the minutes above +8.0 C that the customer's stability letter allows for the lot, minus the minutes already used in this and every earlier excursion on the same lot.

2.2. A lot with an SBR below 30 minutes is not conditionally released. It is held pending external decision.

2.3. The SBR and the letter reference are written on QCL-F-31.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

answer_text:
## Consequences

The decision should be reviewed no earlier than April 2026 unless three major
alert failures occur in a single quarter. A major alert failure means patient
critical stock, no automatic alert to Fleet Control or QA, and a confirmed
temperature breach.

IT must maintain an export script for Kalpa reports. QA must note that Kalpa
uses five-minute polling and may require interpolation in timelines. Fleet must
continue keeping paper driver call logs because Kalpa's door-open event is not
trusted during poor network coverage.

Col. Sandhu's closing comment: "We will not chase a fashionable dashboard while
our drivers and auditors know the present one. STABILITY FIRST; NOVELTY SECOND."

## Consequences

IT retires the Kalpa export script on 30 April 2026. The Kalpa tablet in the
Nagpur guard cabin is a read-only audit device and must not be used to open
alarms. Training material and the QA audit binder are reissued with Tessaline
screenshots before the 2026 vaccine season.

Fleet continues to keep paper driver call logs. That practice survived the
vendor change because network coverage, not the vendor, was the reason for it.

Sandhu's closing comment: "THE DASHBOARD CHANGED; THE DISCIPLINE DOES NOT."

## Review trigger

The review trigger is intentionally narrow. Complaints about dashboard colour,
slow training, or ordinary device replacement do not count as major alert
failures. A review may still be started by the Managing Director, but this ADR
does not require one unless the patient-critical alert threshold above is met.

## What the door sensor showed

The shift's Door Open Minutes (DOM) for C2 were 96, the highest recorded since Tessaline went live, because loading continued during the drill.

## Scenario

A simulated high alarm in C2, with the Tessaline export deliberately withheld for the first 40 minutes so the team had to work without the electronic record. At the same time a milk crate was burst in the rear compartment of RF-118.

## Findings

1. One shift lead emailed the old qa-shared mailbox before calling Compliance-Red. The obsolete habit is named here, as clause 10.4 of the SOP requires: **qa-shared is not an escalation route.**
2. The red sleeve on RF-118 had no spare logger.
3. The night controller paused his run through [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md) when the alarm sounded; no vehicle left during the drill.
4. Two staff asked what "warm pallet" means. It is defined in [the jargon sheet](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

## Reasons

The pilot met its acceptance tests. The C2 sensor tracked the USB logger within
0.3 C. Night alerts reached Compliance-Red in the 18 March 2026 test call, which
was the condition Revathi Iyer set after the March 2025 vaccine excursion.

Kalpa's five-minute polling required interpolation in every investigation
timeline. Sixty-second polling removed that argument from three customer
disputes in the first quarter of parallel running.

The local-service argument that carried the 2023 decision no longer holds.
Tessaline's Nagpur field team replaced two truck devices within one working day
during the January 2026 cold wave.

## Reasons

Kalpa has local service staff within Nagpur city limits and has historically
replaced failed truck devices within one working day. The Nagpur base station is
already mounted and wired. Driver training material, customer report templates,
and the QA audit binder already use Kalpa screenshots. Switching all material
before vaccine season would create training risk.

The Kalpa quote is lower than Tessaline's first commercial quote. Tessaline
quoted Rs. 31.20 lakh for migration, device replacement, and API onboarding.
Tessaline also proposed 60-second polling and a richer API, but the API was not
available for our trial vehicles. Kalpa's five-minute polling is not ideal, but
it is known and accepted by current customer annexes.

The exit clause for Kalpa is acceptable only at contract end. Leaving early
would require six months of minimum recurring charges. This is not justified on
the evidence available in November 2023.

Revision 2.0 (10 November 2025) added item 5 after the Tessaline cutover; revision 1.0 of March 2025 used a phone call to the DC manager instead.

Abbreviations follow [the shorthand page](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

2. The body is run empty with its doors shut until the display holds loading temperature, and then held there for the Pre-Cool Hold Time (PCH) set by the qualification record for that route. Where no qualification record exists, the PCH is 45 minutes.

3. The red sleeve is in the cab locker and holds a spare calibrated logger. No logger, no departure: a hand-held thermometer is not a substitute.

4. Where the qualification record requires a backup passive shipper, its SCT is written in the shipper register. A shipper with no SCT entry is not a backup and the run waits.

## 4. Conditions

4.1. PCH 40 minutes before loading at Pune. The 30 minutes of LQ-51 no longer applies.

4.2. Every run carries one validated passive shipper as backup, hired per trip. Its gel packs must have completed their Shipper Conditioning Time (SCT) of 18 hours at +5.0 C before the run is booked.

4.3. A USB logger travels in the load compartment on every run. The tunnel gap is written as missing, never filled.

4.4. Departure checks for this lane are on [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md).

4.5. LQ-53 is valid for the 2026 summer season only.

Record **LQ-53** qualifies one lane for one product class, one season and one vehicle class. Lane records are numbered one after another and the numbers differ by one digit; quote the number printed on the dispatch note, never the lane name alone.

## 6. After the washdown

5.2. The shift lead signs the wash register QCL-F-40. The driver may do the washdown but may not sign it.

## At the gate

5. A test alarm is sent to Compliance-Red from the vehicle's Tessaline unit, and the QA night phone confirms receipt before the seal goes on.

6. If the Tessaline unit has not reported for 5 consecutive minutes, the vehicle does not leave.

7. Diesel is at least three-quarters of a tank, and the reefer unit's own fuel tank is full.

8. The seal is photographed with the dock clock in frame.

# Reefer Body Washdown and Sanitation Procedure

## 1. When a washdown is required

1.1. After any dairy spill in the body, before the next load.

1.2. Before a chilled body carries pharma critical stock after any food load.

1.3. Every 14 days for a body on dairy rotation, whether or not anything spilled.

1.4. After any load rejected by a customer for odour.

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

## 2. Solution and contact

2.1. The floor, walls to 1 metre, door gaskets and drain channel are wetted with chlorine solution at 200 ppm, mixed fresh for each body.

2.2. The Chlorine Contact Time (CCT) is 10 minutes: the solution stays wet on the surface for that long before rinsing. Wiping the surface dry sooner restarts the count.

2.3. Rinse with potable water, then dry with the doors open and the drain plug out.

## 4. Immediate containment

4.1. Stop movement of the affected pallet, tote, crate, reefer body, or room bay.
Do not load additional customer stock into the affected compartment.

4.2. Attach a red sleeve to the stock or truck file. The red sleeve contains the
customer intimation form, red hold tags, seal tape, and one spare calibrated
logger. If there is no physical sleeve, print form QCL-F-09 and write RED
SLEEVE MISSING at the top.

4.3. Move warehouse stock to quarantine bay Q-3 at Nagpur, Q-G2 at Guwahati, or
Q-C1 at Coimbatore. Truck stock must remain sealed unless QA instructs unloading
for product safety.

4.4. Photograph the sensor display, seal number, dock clock, and pallet labels.
The first four photographs must be uploaded before anyone debates stock
disposition. Do not wait for the manager to arrive.

4.5. Do not warm, chill, re-ice, ventilate, or hide the probe in order to make a
display look normal. Corrective measures may protect product, but the record
must continue to show the product environment honestly.

4.6. If a reefer unit is unstable on the road, the driver shall stop at a lit
fuel plaza or toll rest area, call Fleet Control, and keep the engine running
unless there is a fire, police order, or personal safety threat.

## Appendix A: local contacts

At Nagpur, the DC manager is Farhan Qureshi and the night shift escalation lead
is Bunty Chauhan. At Guwahati, the nominated escalation contact is Riniki
Bora. At Coimbatore, the nominated escalation contact is S. Venkatesan.

During business hours, QA desk extension 440 answers routine excursion queries.
During night shift, the shift lead opens the event and calls Compliance-Red for
pharma critical stock. A new driver who sees a reefer alarm must call Fleet
Control first and must not wait until reaching the destination.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

## 4. Frozen bodies

4.1. A frozen body such as RF-120 is never washed with water while the body is below 0 C. It is dry-wiped with food-grade alcohol, and gets a full washdown only when defrosted at service.

4.2. A raw chicken spill in a frozen body is the exception: the body is taken out of service and defrosted for a full washdown within 24 hours.

## 5. Where and who

5.1. Nagpur: the wash bay beside the generator room. Guwahati: the contract garage. Coimbatore: the wash pad inside the south gate.

5.2. The shift lead signs the wash register QCL-F-40. The driver may do the washdown but may not sign it.

## Languages

Hindi and Marathi at Nagpur, Assamese and Hindi at Guwahati, Tamil at Coimbatore. English slides are available but are not a substitute for a trainer in the local language.

## 6. After the washdown

6.1. A washed body is not loaded until it has been chilled again from empty; the dispatch checklist for the load sets how long.

| module | who | length | month |
|---|---|---|---|
| M4 Washdown | wash bay staff, drivers on dairy rotation | 1 hour | May |

## Module notes

- **M2** walks through [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md) on a real vehicle at the gate. A controller may not dispatch a night pharma run alone until Col. Sandhu or the Fleet head's deputy has signed the practical.
- **M3** covers how stock leaves quarantine under [the green binder](31-quarantine-release-and-return-procedure.md), including when the quarantine dwell limit forces an escalation. Written test, pass mark 80%. Drivers do not attend M3; they never release stock.
- **M4** uses [the Sunday sheet](32-reefer-washdown-and-sanitation-procedure.md). Each trainee times one full CCT with a stopwatch on a real body before signing off.
- **M5** shows planners how each factor of the lane risk score is marked and why dead zones are scored at all.
- **M6** gives every new joiner [the house word list](33-cold-chain-glossary.md) in their first week and 30 minutes with a shift lead to go through it.

## 10. Closure

10.1. The QA head or nominated deputy closes pharma critical investigations. The
DC manager may close dairy and frozen investigations only after QA records the
disposition.

10.2. Corrective and preventive actions must have an owner, a due date, and
evidence of completion. "Discussed on call" is not completion evidence.

10.3. Training actions shall be assigned by role, not by name alone, so that new
staff receive the same correction.

10.4. The case file must be kept for seven years for pharma critical stock and
three years for food stock.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

# Quarantine Stock Release and Return Procedure

How stock leaves quarantine bays Q-3 (Nagpur), Q-G2 (Guwahati) and Q-C1 (Coimbatore) after QA has recorded a disposition under clause 6.5 of the [Temperature Excursion Response SOP](01-sop-temperature-excursion.md). Destroyed stock does not leave by this procedure; section 7 of that SOP governs it.

## 2. Conditional release of pharma stock

2.1. Before a conditional release QA calculates the Stability Budget Remaining (SBR): the minutes above +8.0 C that the customer's stability letter allows for the lot, minus the minutes already used in this and every earlier excursion on the same lot.

2.2. A lot with an SBR below 30 minutes is not conditionally released. It is held pending external decision.

2.3. The SBR and the letter reference are written on QCL-F-31.

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

2. The body is run empty with its doors shut until the display holds loading temperature, and then held there for the Pre-Cool Hold Time (PCH) set by the qualification record for that route. Where no qualification record exists, the PCH is 45 minutes.

3. The red sleeve is in the cab locker and holds a spare calibrated logger. No logger, no departure: a hand-held thermometer is not a substitute.

4. Where the qualification record requires a backup passive shipper, its SCT is written in the shipper register. A shipper with no SCT entry is not a backup and the run waits.

## 10. Training and drills

10.1. Every warehouse shift lead, fleet controller, and customer service agent
who handles cold-chain accounts must complete excursion training once each
calendar year. New joiners must complete the same training before they are
assigned unsupervised night duty.

10.2. Nagpur shall run one night-shift drill every quarter because it is the
central hub and handles the largest mix of pharma, dairy, and frozen movements.
Guwahati and Coimbatore shall each run at least two drills per year. A drill
must include one missing-record problem, not only a simple high-temperature
alarm.

10.3. Training records must show attendance, scenario, trainer, questions raised
by staff, and any local confusion found during the drill. Repeating a slide deck
without recording staff questions is not enough evidence for this SOP.

10.4. If a drill finds that staff are using a shortcut, hiding an alarm, calling
the wrong group, or relying on an obsolete document, QA must open a corrective
action. The corrective action may be simple, but it must name the obsolete habit
plainly.

## 6. Investigation record

6.1. QA opens an investigation in QCL-F-17 before the end of the same shift. The
record must contain the sensor source, product owner, SKU, batch or lot number,
route, room, dock, seal number, driver name when applicable, and first staff
member who observed the event.

6.2. The investigator shall build a minute-level timeline from the approved
temperature record, door log, dock schedule, driver call log, maintenance ticket,
and shift handover note. Missing pieces must be listed as missing; do not fill
them with assumptions.

6.3. Where records conflict, use the source hierarchy in section 3 and explain
the conflict. A convenient record is not a better record.

6.4. For pharma critical stock, QA must ask the customer for a stability letter
before release when the product was above the high limit or below the low limit
for any confirmed duration.

6.5. The investigation shall name one of four dispositions: release, conditional
release, hold pending external decision, or destroy. Finance may record value
only after QA records the disposition.

## 8. Dock and staging rules

8.1. A dock is not a temperature-controlled room. Staging time begins when the
pallet crosses the cold-room threshold and ends when the reefer body is closed
or the pallet returns to the cold room.

8.2. Pharma pallets may not be staged on an open dock for more than 10 minutes
unless a validated passive shipper is used.

8.3. Dairy pallets may be staged on a covered dock for loading, but the dairy
high-excursion rule in clause 2.3 still applies. Staff shall not reclassify
staging time as "not cold chain time" after the fact.

8.4. Frozen stock must move directly between freezer and reefer body. Any delay
longer than 8 minutes must be called to the shift lead.

8.5. The dock team may request a slot change, but it may not waive a temperature
limit. Only QA may decide whether an excursion occurred.

# Quillfern Cold Chain Glossary

Plain meanings for expressions used on site. Short forms are defined in the document that uses them, never here, so an expression below appears in its long form only.

back-to-cold — the moment a staged pallet crosses back over the cold-room threshold; staging time stops here.
chlorine contact time — the minutes a sanitising solution must stay wet on a reefer floor before rinsing; wiping it dry early starts the count again.
dead zone — a stretch of road where the telematics unit cannot report; the USB logger covers it and the gap is recorded as missing, never filled in.
door open minutes — the total minutes a cold-room or reefer door stood open in one shift, summed from the door sensor; a measure of load, not a fault.
holding lane B — the covered waiting lane at Nagpur for pharma and frozen vehicles that miss their dock time; nothing is unloaded there.
mean kinetic temperature — the single steady temperature that would give stock the same total heat stress as the uneven record it actually saw; stability letters are written against it, not against the average.
pre-cool hold time — the minutes an empty reefer body is held at loading temperature, doors shut, before the first pallet goes in.
probe grid — the layout of loggers used when a room is mapped; each position is named by rack, bay and height, such as A1-high.
relief point — a named fuel plaza or rest area on a qualified route where a relief driver or a mobile service van can meet the vehicle.
seal watch — time a driver spends guarding a sealed vehicle; it is duty time and never counts as rest.
shipper conditioning time — the hours a passive shipper's gel packs must sit at their set temperature before the shipper may leave with stock.
stability budget remaining — the minutes above the high limit that a customer's stability letter still allows for one lot, once every earlier excursion on that lot is subtracted.
warm pallet — night-shift name for a pallet whose logger has alarmed but whose excursion QA has not yet confirmed; it is handled as quarantine stock until QA decides.
white tag — the RELEASED tag fixed beside a red hold tag when QA lets stock out of quarantine; the red tag stays on.

## Before loading

1. Two drivers are named on the dispatch note before departure, as clause 2.3 of the [Driver Hours and Road Safety Policy](08-driver-hours-and-safety-policy.md) requires.

2. The body is run empty with its doors shut until the display holds loading temperature, and then held there for the Pre-Cool Hold Time (PCH) set by the qualification record for that route. Where no qualification record exists, the PCH is 45 minutes.

3. The red sleeve is in the cab locker and holds a spare calibrated logger. No logger, no departure: a hand-held thermometer is not a substitute.

4. Where the qualification record requires a backup passive shipper, its SCT is written in the shipper register. A shipper with no SCT entry is not a backup and the run waits.

## Summary

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of

## 4. Speed and conduct

4.1. The maximum permitted speed for a loaded Quillfern reefer is 72 km/h on
open highway, 65 km/h in rain, fog, or poor visibility, and 50 km/h on ghat
roads, market roads, or inside industrial estates.

4.2. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited except through a hands-free
device for Fleet Control calls. Messaging, app troubleshooting, and customer
calls must be handled while parked.

4.3. Alcohol, intoxicants, and sedating medicines not declared to Fleet Control
are prohibited. The limit is zero during duty and for eight hours before duty.

4.4. Seat belts are mandatory for driver and passenger. A route assistant who
travels without a belt must be reported as a safety non-conformance, not treated
as a local habit.

4.5. Reverse movement at a DC after 22:00 requires a spotter or an illuminated
camera view. If lighting fails, movement stops until safe guidance is available.

# Driver hours and safety policy — Vantorix

## 1. Daily limits

1.1. A driver may drive at most 8 hours in any period of
24 hours, extended to 11 hours no more than twice a week.

1.2. A break of at least 30 minutes is taken after
5 hours of driving. The break is not taken at a dock while
waiting for a slot.

# Driver hours and safety policy — Zephyrine

## 1. Daily limits

1.1. A driver may drive at most 8 hours in any period of
24 hours, extended to 11 hours no more than twice a week.

1.2. A break of at least 45 minutes is taken after
5 hours of driving. The break is not taken at a dock while
waiting for a slot.

## 3. Exceptions

3.1. If weather, police stoppage, road closure, civil disturbance, vehicle
breakdown, medical emergency, or a safety threat would cause a driver to exceed
a limit, the driver must stop at the nearest lit fuel plaza, toll rest area,
police post, customer secure yard, or Quillfern DC.

3.2. Fleet Control shall log the exception under code SANDHU-EXC with the time,
place, reason, stock type, driver statement, and revised plan. The exception is
not closed until a rest plan is recorded.

3.3. A cold-chain emergency is not by itself a driving-hours exception. The
correct response is to secure the vehicle, protect the product, and arrange a
replacement driver, mobile service, or customer-approved transfer.

3.4. Managers shall not instruct a driver to "push through", "make up time", or
"just reach the next DC" after the legal or Quillfern limit is reached. Such an
instruction is misconduct even when no crash occurs.

## 1. Scope

1.1. The policy applies to owned reefers, hired reefers, support vans, escort
cars used for pharma critical movement, and any vehicle carrying Quillfern staff
between a DC, customer site, toll plaza, hotel, or repair yard.

1.2. A driver is on duty from the first required report at gate, yard, hotel, or
customer premises until the vehicle is parked, keys are handed over or secured,
documents are deposited, and the driver is released by Fleet Control.

1.3. A customer request, delayed dock slot, vaccine urgency, milk spoilage risk,
or senior manager's impatience does not cancel this policy. NO LOAD IS WORTH A
LIFE.

## Rooms

- After the March re-mapping (TMS-44), the permanent C2 sensor was moved to the new worst case probe position. Bunty's team confirmed the move on 2 April 2026.

## Root cause

The immediate cause was warm air ingress through a torn door curtain and door
opening during dairy cross-dock spillover. The deeper cause was that the Kalpa
alert routing still pointed to the old qa-shared mailbox, which was not watched
by the night team. The shift lead tried to protect the room by placing dry ice
near the curtain, but the team did not quarantine stock until the manager was
awake.

We also found that dock scheduling pushed paneer loading next to the vaccine
cold-room door. This did not create the torn curtain, but it increased door
traffic during the vulnerable period. The dock plan must separate pharma
loading from dairy overflow during night shift.

## Timeline

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 02:16 | Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 recorded +9.1 C in cold room C2. |

## Summary

At approximately 02:16 on 12 March 2025, Kalpa probe KV-NGP-C2-07 began
reporting a high temperature in C2, the vaccine cold room at Nagpur DC. The
affected consignment was BharatVac order BV-4437, holding 18,400 vials of
rotavirus vaccine in lots ROTA-9A and ROTA-9B. The approved record showed the
room above +8.0 C for 66 minutes. At the time of the event, the SOP required a
QA call after 30 continuous minutes above +8.0 C for vaccines. The current
corrective action is to reduce that duration.

## Findings

1. One shift lead emailed the old qa-shared mailbox before calling Compliance-Red. The obsolete habit is named here, as clause 10.4 of the SOP requires: **qa-shared is not an escalation route.**
2. The red sleeve on RF-118 had no spare logger.
3. The night controller paused his run through [the pink card](30-pharma-night-dispatch-checklist.md) when the alarm sounded; no vehicle left during the drill.
4. Two staff asked what "warm pallet" means. It is defined in [the jargon sheet](33-cold-chain-glossary.md).

## What the door sensor showed

The shift's Door Open Minutes (DOM) for C2 were 96, the highest recorded since Tessaline went live, because loading continued during the drill.

## 3. Swab check

3.1. Three swabs: floor front, floor rear, door gasket.
